request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Printing the Squares of Numbers Within a Specified Range (Case 1) [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program to write out the squares of even positive integers less than or equal to 10. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Iterate through the numbers in the sequence [[LINE02]] for num in range(2, 11, 2): [[LINE03]] #Step 1.1: Square and print each number in the sequence [[LINE04]] print(num, "squared =", num * num) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to repeat the same process for each of the even positive integers that are less than or equal to 10. To do this, we need to use a loop structure. We use for loops instead of a while loop because we need to repeat the loop a certain number of times, and for loops are best-suited in cases like this when we know ahead of time the number of times that we need to repeat the loop.

We use the range function because it generates a sequence of numbers for the for loop. Here, we want a sequence that starts at 2 (2 is the first positive even number) with every even integer number up to but not including 11. We get this sequence by calling the function range(2,11,2). [[LINE02.EXPL2]] The last number in the range function specifies how much to increase each successive integer in the sequence, if this is omitted then step defaults to 1. Since we want to print only every even integer numbers, we set the step to 2.

Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] In each iteration of the loop, this statement prints the square number to the default standard output stream. To square each number in the sequence, we multiply it by itself using the multiplication (*) operator.

Note that we do not necessarily have to store the squared number in a variable. The multiplication may also be performed directly in the print statement. [[LINE04.EXPL2]] The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]] [[DIST1.LC]] for num in range(1, 11, 4): [[DIST2.LC]] for num in range(1, 10, 2): [[DIST3.LC]] for num in range(2, 10, 1): [[DIST4.LC]] for num in range(2, 11, 3): [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]] Translate the given worked example into Arabic. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.
